claim: On May 7, 2015, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit held that the NSA's bulk telephone-metadata program — the one the Verizon order revealed — was illegal, ruling that it "exceeds the scope of what Congress has authorized and therefore violates Section 215" of the Patriot Act. Congress let the bulk-collection authority lapse weeks later, replacing it with the more limited USA Freedom Act on June 2, 2015.

sources.label: ACLU v. Clapper, 785 F.3d 787 (2d Cir. May 7, 2015), opinion by Judge Gerard E. Lynch.
sources.quote: the telephone metadata program exceeds the scope of what Congress has authorized and therefore violates Section 215.

sources.label: Electronic Frontier Foundation — "ACLU v. Clapper and the Congress: How The Second Circuit's Decision Affects the Legislative Landscape" (May 8, 2015).

notes: Group A. Year 2015, filed under the y2013 Snowden anchor because it is the legal resolution of the Verizon §215 order in 2013-verizon-215-order-001 — the program the leak exposed was ruled unlawful. Court opinion url left null per source hygiene (Justia/FindLaw both 403 to the fetcher); the holding language is verbatim and the EFF link is the live secondary. The ruling closed the §215 bulk-telephony question; it did not reach §702/PRISM, which remains operational.
